topics.inclusion_rule: Studies that verify or identify a user from speech-production signals (voice, whisper, non-audible murmur, lip or face motion, articulatory or active-acoustic sensing, imagined-speech EEG), found by authentication, speaker or user verification/identification, biometric or impostor wording in the ledger; the design compared is how a user is enrolled and how impostor data and the decision threshold are obtained (enrollment session, impostor or background-speaker data, few-shot enrollment, threshold calibration). Boundary: surveys, datasets and studies that only mention biometrics count as pattern matches; attended-speaker detection in EEG is not verification; a study counts under every design its full text names; versions count once.

Studies that emit an acoustic signal (near-ultrasonic or ultrasonic, from a loudspeaker, earphone or transducer) and decode speech, silent speech or mouth state from its reflection or Doppler shift off the lips, face, jaw or vocal tract, captured by a microphone. Boundary: B-mode ultrasound tongue imaging, RF radar, Wi-Fi and laser sensing are excluded when read; reviews and datasets without a decoding result count as pattern matches only; versions of one study count once.

Same population as active-acoustic-speech-sensing (emitted near-ultrasonic or ultrasonic signal, reflection decoded for speech or mouth state); the design compared is where the transducers sit (in-ear, earphone or headphone; glasses or headset; smartphone or loudspeaker) and whether a voiced or whispered audio stream is fused with the echo. Boundary: a study counts under every design its full text names (upper bound); surveys and datasets count as pattern matches only.

Same verification population as the M03 topic; the design compared is the identity model: GMM/HMM classifiers, GMM-UBM or i-/x-vector back-ends, metric-learning embeddings (triplet, contrastive, angular margin, siamese), cross-modal alignment between two streams, and a multi-task or shared encoder that also serves content recognition. Boundary: a study counts under every design its full text names (upper bound); a related-work mention counts as a match.

Same verification population as the M03 topic; the design compared is what the deployed system returns: an identity decision only, or decoded content (word, digit, password, command) together with an identity decision from the same utterance; also whether silent or unvoiced input, EER and attack or liveness tests are named. Boundary: content and identity produced by separately trained stages still count as joint output; a study counts under every design its full text names.

Same population as active-acoustic-speech-sensing; the design compared is how the reported test set is separated from training: user-held-out (leave-one-user-out or cross-user), session- or day-held-out, or a random sample split. Boundary: a paper counts under every protocol its text names; reviews count as pattern matches only.
